lead.headline: Trump says the Iran war is "militarily effectively over" and holds off new strikes, though the US is "locked and loaded"
lead.byline: THE HINDU · THE TIMES OF INDIA · 10 NOV
lead.short: Donald Trump said on Monday that the war with Iran was "militarily effectively over" and that new strikes did not seem necessary for now, after appeals from Gulf states including Qatar, whose prime minister he met at the White House. "We're just keeping it the status quo," he said, adding that the US was "locked and loaded" if anything changed.

why.text: It is the clearest signal yet that Washington wants out of an eight-month war that has pushed up fuel prices worldwide, including in India.

more: Trump said Iran had been "decapitated" but that he still wanted a long-term deal to make sure its nuclear programme was defanged, and spoke of "positive momentum" towards ending the war. Iran continues to block at least part of the traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. His Republican Party lost both chambers of Congress last week, in elections shadowed by anger over the war.

The US evacuated aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in Britain on Monday after a threat from Iran, The Wall Street Journal reported. In Tehran, Mohsen Rezaei told Washington to stop "making up news about imaginary negotiations" and to "surrender to Iran's seven conditions" for ending the war.

facts.Mildenhall: US aircraft moved after an Iranian threat, per the WSJ

update.new: Trump calls the war militarily over and holds off strikes.
update.front: Trump now says the Iran war is over in all but name.

seconds.headline: Trump says the FBI is looking into Jensen Huang's affair, and that Huang told him he had "no idea she was a spy"
seconds.short: Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI was looking into the affair between Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy. Trump said he asked Huang whether he knew. "He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump said, calling him an "honourable guy".

why.text: An FBI inquiry raises the stakes for the company whose chips power the AI boom, and for the investors already suing it.

more: The news knocked about $250bn off Nvidia's value on Monday as its shares fell more than 4%. Shareholders have sued Nvidia and Huang over the affair, The Guardian reported. China's foreign ministry called the claims "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". Trump did not say when the FBI inquiry began.

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is not related to Jensen Huang. She was managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore company that has dealt with Nvidia. Marco Rubio sent officials a memo in the spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy, according to The New York Times.

update.new: The FBI is involved, shareholders sue and Nvidia loses about $250bn in value.
update.front: The Huang affair is now an FBI matter.

seconds.headline: Sonia Gandhi's memoir calls the Emergency a mistake and says Modi avoids eye contact, and the BJP calls it 'whitewashing'
seconds.short: Sonia Gandhi's memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", was released on Tuesday, and in it she calls the Emergency of 1975 a mistake. The BJP said the book should have been titled "Whitewashing". Gandhi also writes that she has no real contact with Narendra Modi, who "tends to look away, avoiding eye contact".

why.text: It is the most personal account yet from the woman who led the Congress for two decades, published as her party looks for a way back.

more: The book recalls Rahul Gandhi's words before Rajiv Gandhi's assassination: "I'll have to come back for his funeral." It also describes encounters with world leaders, including Bill Clinton's "roving eye", Nicolas Sarkozy's arrogance and Princess Diana's warmth. In an interview with The Hindu before the launch, she said the BJP had done "great damage" to the fabric of India.

BJP spokesperson C.R. Kesavan said the book was "sugar-coating the historical wrongs perpetrated" by the Nehru-Gandhi family. He asked whether she had wept for the victims of the 1984 Sikh massacre or the 26/11 Mumbai attacks, and called her account of the Emergency "truly appalling".

update.new: The memoir is out, and the BJP attacks it.
update.front: The book is now out, and its account of the Emergency has started a new fight with the BJP.

seconds.headline: Rain washes out the third ODI in Hamilton after a day of waiting, and India keep their 2-0 series lead
seconds.byline: THE TIMES OF INDIA · ESPNCRICINFO · 10 NOV
seconds.short: The third ODI between New Zealand and India at Seddon Park in Hamilton was abandoned on Tuesday after persistent rain and repeated delays. Shubman Gill won the toss when the weather briefly cleared and revised timings were set, but another spell of rain sent the players off for good. India still lead the five-match series 2-0.

why.text: India need one more win from the last two games, both in Mount Maunganui, to take the series.

more: The Indian team bus reached the ground 30 minutes before the start, but only Rohit Sharma got off, to talk to the operations teams. Players who entered the players' and officials' area would not have been allowed to leave and come back, so the team returned to the hotel as drizzle continued and New Zealand's players drove back too.

When the outfield was readied in quick time, the squads returned, with Rohit travelling in New Zealand's car. Families, including Rohit's wife Ritika and the parents of Gill and Arshdeep Singh, had taken their seats in the hospitality box. The fourth ODI is on Friday at 07:30 IST.

facts.series: India lead 2-0 with two to play
facts.next: 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui, Fri 13 Nov 07:30 IST

update.new: The third ODI was washed out.
update.front: India's series lead survives a Hamilton washout.

stories.headline: Russia, Ukraine and the US open their first real peace talks since February in Abu Dhabi, and India offers to help
stories.short: Russian, Ukrainian and US negotiators began two days of talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, the first substantive negotiations between Moscow and Kyiv since February. US officials said they would seek a "final end" to the war, including a "long-term security architecture" between Russia and Europe and possibly guarantees for Ukraine "very similar to Nato".

why.text: A US offer of Nato-like guarantees, and the chance of lifting sanctions on Russia, would reshape Europe's security and India's oil trade.

more: A US official said Washington would "need Europe at the table" and that negotiators could revive the Nato-Russia council, suspended after the 2022 invasion, and possibly lift sanctions on Russia. Russia has strongly opposed Nato admitting Ukraine. European officials fear Russia will insist that Nato pull back its forces from eastern Europe.

On Monday Narendra Modi spoke to Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said India was ready to mediate between Russia and Ukraine to set up "food corridors". S. Jaishankar then spoke to Russia's foreign minister, Sergey Lavrov, the clearest sign yet of the go-between role New Delhi is now playing between Moscow and Kyiv.

facts.talks: two days in Abu Dhabi from Tuesday
facts.India: offered to help set up food corridors

update.new: The talks have begun, with a US offer of Nato-like guarantees.

stories.headline: A Republican congressman forces a House vote on impeaching Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, within 48 hours
stories.short: Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced articles of impeachment against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on the House floor on Monday, starting a 48-hour clock for a vote. "By engaging in hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorisation, Secretary Hegseth is breaking the law," Massie said. Hegseth has called the effort a "sham".

why.text: It is unlikely to pass, but it is a first test of how far Republicans will defend the war after losing Congress.

more: Republicans control Congress until January, so the effort is expected to fail. Massie, who lost re-election this year, said he wanted to push Trump to replace Hegseth with someone who could be confirmed quickly before Democrats take over. "My effort to impeach Secretary Hegseth is a much gentler version of what's coming," he said.

The House can vote on the resolution directly, send it to committee or set it aside. Hegseth called Massie a "disgruntled, defeated congressman". "They attack us because we are effective," he said in a video. "We will not back down." In 250 years, the US has impeached only two cabinet secretaries.

facts.Massie's charge: hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without authorisation

stories.headline: Brent crude falls to its lowest since August as Trump steps back from strikes, while Indian markets close for Balipratipada
stories.short: Brent crude fell 24 cents to $92.33 a barrel early on Tuesday, after settling 5.85% lower on Monday at its lowest since 31 August, as Donald Trump said new strikes on Iran were not necessary for now. Indian stock exchanges are shut on Tuesday for Diwali-Balipratipada, and trading resumes on Wednesday.

why.text: Cheaper oil has driven India's rally and the rupee's recovery, and Wednesday's open will show whether that holds.

more: US West Texas Intermediate fell 35 cents to $86.50. Trump held off after appeals from countries in the region, including from Qatar's prime minister. OPEC's output rose in October, led by Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq, despite continued limits on exports, a Reuters survey found. Iran still blocks at least part of the traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

The Sensex and Nifty rose more than 6% over the last five sessions to their highest closes in more than eight months, Mint reported, helped by falling crude, renewed foreign buying and better global sentiment. The Multi Commodity Exchange is shut for the morning session and opens from 5pm to 11.30pm.

update.new: Brent at its lowest since August.

notes.Sensex: Markets are shut today; the Sensex closed Monday up 0.1% at 81,107, its highest close in three months.
notes.Brent crude: About $90.50, down 2.3%, its lowest since late August.
notes.Nasdaq-100: Rose 3.4% on Monday as tech shares recovered.

stories.headline: Anthropic releases two new Claude models and pushes ahead with a listing it hopes to start trading next week
stories.short: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 on Monday and said Claude Mythos 5.2 would go first to vetted organisations, claiming gains in coding, reasoning and vision over the 5.1 models from September. The company plans to set a valuation range for its stock market listing this week and begin trading next Thursday or Friday, The Wall Street Journal reported.

why.text: Investors will read Anthropic's valuation as a test of the AI boom after a week of falling tech shares.

more: In testing, the models "helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes" and "formalized the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours", Anthropic said. Fable 5.2 can direct teams of AI agents on long-running projects, it said.

Some institutional investors are pushing for a valuation below the $1.5 trillion discussed as recently as last week, itself well below the $2 trillion floated a few months ago, the Journal reported. The listing comes shortly after one of the Nasdaq's biggest sell-offs and the Nvidia scandal.

facts.trading: planned for next Thursday or Friday, per the WSJ

update.new: New models, and the listing is back on for next week.

stories.headline: Manchester United are expected to sack Michael Carrick after their worst start to a top-flight season in 40 years
stories.short: Manchester United look increasingly likely to sack head coach Michael Carrick during the international break, BBC Sport reports. Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are expected to recommend his dismissal to Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family. Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left United 18th, with one league win in 10.

why.text: United would be looking for their next manager during the season again, with Liverpool up next after the break.

more: The club stuck with Carrick after a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October, planning to reassess during the break. Multiple sources told the BBC no final decision had been made. The Villa draw was Carrick's third match since then: a win, a draw and a defeat, with United twice coming back from two goals down.

United have sounded out Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, the BBC reported in October. Antonio Conte is keen on the job, and Mauricio Pochettino is open to a move, though he extended his contract as USA coach in August. Carrick, 45, signed a two-year deal last summer.

update.new: The club is expected to sack Carrick.

screen.title: Resident Evil
